name: Bangladesh
headline: Bangladesh: +3.5% growth in 2025, 10.0% inflation, debt 42% of GDP
sections: Bangladesh is a $458 billion economy (2025), the world's 37th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +3.5% in 2025, close to the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $10K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 22.4% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose 10.0% in 2025, above typical targets, up from 6.1% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 3.8% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 9.4% (2025).
Gross government debt is 42% of GDP (2025), a moderate level that has risen from 35% in 2020. The general government balance is −3.1% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is +0.0% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 28% of GDP (2025), a relatively closed economy. Net FDI inflows were 0.4% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 49% of GDP by 2031, still rising from today's level. Life expectancy is 74.9 years (2024). Population: 173.7 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
